assessment.summary: TREM2 is a well-characterized immunoreceptor with excellent structural data (15 PDB entries at up to 1.47Å, 11 with bound ligands) confirming a tractable ligand-binding site. Although ChEMBL currently records zero IC50 entries, a 2026 first-in-human study of an oral small-molecule TREM2 agonist (VG-3927/SAR448851) demonstrates real chemical tractability not yet reflected in public databases. The target has strong disease validation across Alzheimer's disease, cancer, and infectious disease, supporting a medium druggability rating with an upward trajectory as clinical data matures.
evidence_gaps: ChEMBL has zero IC50 entries despite emerging small-molecule chemical matter in clinical development — significant database lag
No approved drugs; clinical validation of small-molecule agonist approach still pending
Agonism of a cell-surface immune receptor is mechanistically complex; full MoA of small-molecule agonists not publicly characterized
Structural coverage of transmembrane and intracellular signalling domains is limited; pLDDT only moderate (76.8) suggesting disordered regions
Selectivity profiles of clinical candidates against related TREM family members not publicly available
Pharmacokinetic and CNS penetration data for oral small molecules targeting TREM2 in neurodegeneration context is sparse in public literature
